entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Licinius Lucullus was a Roman politician who became consul in 151 BC. He rose to prominence during the First Mithridatic War and played a key role in the Roman conquest of Pontic territories.

As commander of the Roman forces, Lucullus employed innovative tactics that allowed him to defeat the Armenian general Tigranes II at the Battle of Tissaphernes in 69 BC. His victories led to the capture of several important cities, including Miletus and Satala.

Despite his successes on the battlefield, Lucullus faced criticism for his handling of the war in Asia Minor. He was accused of being too lenient towards the local population, which ultimately led to his recall to Rome.

Lucullus' legacy extends beyond his military campaigns. He was a patron of the arts and architecture, and his influence can be seen in the development of Roman architecture during the Late Republic period.

The Lucullan style, named after him, characterized by its use of domed buildings and ornate decoration, became a hallmark of Roman architecture during this time.

Lucullus' life serves as an example of the complexities and nuances of Roman politics and military strategy. His legacy continues to fascinate historians and scholars today.
